title: Attention implementations
tasks: Build the compiled MLX baseline

Use optimized GQA and an additive relative bias. Test batch-to-head sink equivalence against a dense reference, include mask construction and cache updates, and confirm the fast path or label the fallback.
In progress
Compiled MLX and GPU parity tests are implemented. Host checks passed for batched sink/head folding. Running the optimized path and reviewing its dispatches awaits GPU access.
Build staged Metal
Implement preparation, KV scan and gate with a common native math core and preallocated buffers. Encode into one ordered command buffer and verify intermediate and final state.
In progress
The Objective-C++ host bridge compiled and loaded. Staged Metal encodes preparation, scan and gate in one command buffer. GPU shader compilation and output parity remain open.
Build the single-dispatch Metal kernel
Give each sequence/KV-head pair exclusive write ownership. Stage only live tiles, use online softmax and record compiled resource limits. Require parity with the staged path.
In progress
The shader forwards the rounded current K/V pair through threadgroup memory and streams older K/V tiles. GPU execution and parity remain open.
Build the hybrid schedule
Combine native preparation with tuned MLX attention and gating in the same calling context. Verify ownership and dependencies and charge any interop copies, layout changes and synchronization.
In progress
Implemented the custom Metal preparation shader, MLX cache append, tuned SDPA and output gate. Host numerical checks passed. GPU compilation, trace and parity remain open.
Check the parallelism explanation
Implement a native split-context scan and numerically stable merge. Count the sink and current token once. Test 64 and 4,096 positions and capture traces for the matched and split variants.
In progress
Implemented the split-context scan and stable merge with one sink contribution. GPU timings and dispatch traces remain open.
